definition_en: a burrowing mammal with a striped face; also, to pester someone persistently
core_image: 一只獾咬住裤脚不放，甩也甩不掉
scene: 弟弟一路追问个没完，直到姐姐松口。He badgered his sister into lending the car.
sceneCN: 这里 badger 指「纠缠、烦扰」（第 2 个义项：不停追问）；句意：他软磨硬泡，姐姐终于把车借给了他。

derivatives.zh: 蜜獾（复合术语，以凶悍著称）

senses.title: The striped burrowing mammal
senses.definition: a heavy, short-legged mammal with a white-striped face that digs burrows
senses.definitionCN: 体壮腿短、面部有白色条纹、善掘洞的哺乳动物
senses.example: A badger crossed the lane at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一只獾穿过小路。
senses.why: The animal itself is the word's root sense.
senses.whyCN: 动物本身即这个词的本义。

senses.title: To pester persistently
senses.definition: to harass or nag someone repeatedly until they give in
senses.definitionCN: 反复纠缠、唠叨，直至对方让步
senses.example: Reporters badgered the minister about the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们就泄密事件纠缠部长不放。
senses.why: From the baiting sport: dogs pinned a badger in its hole and it fought back without yielding.
senses.whyCN: 源于逗獾游戏：犬在洞口围堵，獾拒不屈服，遂引申出「纠缠」。

senses.title: To urge relentlessly
senses.definition: to press someone with repeated demands or requests
senses.definitionCN: 以反复的要求或恳求催迫某人
senses.example: She badgered the office for a reply all week.
senses.exampleCN: 她整整一周催着办公室要答复。
senses.why: Persistence alone distinguishes it from mere asking.
senses.whyCN: 与普通请求之别只在「不停」。

senses.title: The baited animal in sport
senses.definition: in the old blood sport, the badger drawn from its sett to fight dogs
senses.definitionCN: 旧时血腥游戏里被从洞中诱出与犬相斗的獾
senses.exampleCN: 1835 年议会取缔了逗獾游戏。
senses.why: The verb was born inside this cruel custom.
senses.whyCN: 动词正是在这一残忍习俗中诞生的。

senses.title: Gruff, stubborn character
senses.definition: a person compared to the badger, ill-tempered or reclusive
senses.definitionCN: 被比作獾的人：脾气坏或喜独处
senses.example: The old badger of the village kept to his forge.
senses.exampleCN: 村里那位老倔头整天守着铁匠铺。
senses.why: The animal's surly look lent itself to the likeness.
senses.whyCN: 獾一脸倔相，自然被借来写人。

senses.title: Legal badgering of witnesses
senses.definition: harassing questioning of a witness, as objected in court
senses.definitionCN: 法庭上被异议的纠缠式盘问
senses.example: Counsel objected: the witness was being badgered.
senses.exampleCN: 律师提出异议：证人正受纠缠式盘问。
senses.why: Courtroom procedure froze the verb into a term of art.
senses.whyCN: 法庭程序把这个动词冻结成了术语。

senses.title: The badger game, a swindle
senses.definition: in slang, an extortion trick built on fabricated romance
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中，以虚构恋情为基础的敲诈骗局
senses.example: Victims of the badger game rarely went to the police.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人跳的受害者极少报警。
senses.why: The cornered-baiting image transferred to cornered victims.
senses.whyCN: 「被围堵的獾」意象转用于被围堵的受害者。

senses.title: Honey badger, emblem of grit
senses.definition: the honey badger as a popular emblem of fearless persistence
senses.definitionCN: 蜜獾作为流行文化中无畏坚韧的象征
senses.example: The startup's logo is a honey badger for a reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那家创业公司以蜜獾为标志是有原因的。
senses.why: The animal's refusal to retreat became internet legend.
senses.whyCN: 蜜獾从不后退，遂成网络传奇。

intro.en: Badger the animal probably comes from badge, for the white mark on its forehead, though an older theory links it to a word for a dealer or hawker; the verb grew from the baiting sport of the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 动物义的 badger 一般认为出自 badge「徽章」，指其额部白斑；另有旧说将其与「行商」一词相联。动词义则生长于 16 世纪的逗獾游戏。

items.en: The name bauson was older; badger appears in the early sixteenth century.
items.cn: 更早的名字是 bauson；badger 见于 16 世纪初。

items.en: The white forehead mark suggested badge as the source of the name.
items.cn: 额部白斑使人联想其名出自 badge「徽章」。

items.en: An older theory ties badger to the itinerant dealer who carried goods by badger or bag.
items.cn: 旧说则把 badger 与背负行囊的流动商贩相联。

items.en: In badger-baiting, dogs drew the animal from its hole; the verb to badger arose from this.
items.cn: 逗獾游戏中犬将獾诱出洞穴，动词 to badger 由此而生。

items.en: The verb widened to any persistent pestering or hounding.
items.cn: 17、18 世纪动词义扩大为一切纠缠不休的烦扰。

items.en: The animal survives in countryside and mascot; the verb thrives in news and courtrooms.
items.cn: 动物义存于乡野与吉祥物，动词义活跃于新闻与法庭。

note.en: Group one gathers sound-alikes and the animal's names; group two gathers the pestering family.
note.cn: 第一组收音近词与该动物的别名；第二组收纠缠义场的词。

entries.definition: an emblem or mark; the leading theory of the animal's name.
entries.definitionCN: 徽章、标记；动物命名的主导学说。

entries.definition: the obsolete name for the badger in older English.
entries.definitionCN: 旧英语中獾的废用别名。

entries.definition: the older country name for a badger, surviving in place names.
entries.definitionCN: 乡野旧称，今存于地名，如 Brockenhurst。

entries.definition: to annoy with repeated requests; lighter than badger.
entries.definitionCN: 以重复请求烦扰；语气轻于 badger。

entries.definition: to harass persistently, often in force.
to chase or pursue relentlessly, like a hunting dog.
to scold or complain continuously; domestic register.
to beg persistently and urgently; formal register.

normalIntro.en: Picture a badger tugging your trouser cuff, refusing to let go.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一只獾咬着你的裤脚，说什么也不放。

normal.en: The verb grew from badger baiting: cornered, it never yields.
normal.cn: 动词源于逗獾游戏：被围堵的獾绝不屈服。

normal.en: badger someone into doing is the exam pattern.
normal.cn: badger someone into doing 是考试句型。

normal.en: Courtroom term: badgering the witness draws an objection.
normal.cn: 法庭术语：badgering the witness 会被法官制止。

normal.en: The white forehead stripe explains the badge theory.
normal.cn: 额部白条解释了 badge（徽章）学说。

normal.en: Pair it with hound and pester for the pestering family.
normal.cn: 与 hound、pester 成组记，同属纠缠词族。

abstract.en: Feel the small teeth that do not tire.
abstract.cn: 感受那副不知疲倦的小牙。
纠缠是武装到牙齿的耐心。

abstract.en: Hear the same question for the ninth time.
abstract.cn: 听同一个问题被问到第九遍。

examples.en: The children badgered their father for a puppy all summer.
examples.cn: 孩子们磨了父亲一整个夏天，想要一只小狗。

examples.en: A family of badgers denned under the old barn.
examples.cn: 一窝獾在旧谷仓下安了家。

examples.en: Stop badgering me; I heard you the first time.
examples.cn: 别再烦我了，第一遍我就听见了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「八征」——他八次上门征询答案，磨得人不得安宁

root: 动物义 badger 约 16 世纪初见于英语，主流学说认为出自 badge「徽章」，指其额部白斑；旧说则联系「行商」一词。动词义 16 世纪生长于逗獾游戏（badger-baiting）：獾被犬围堵于洞口而拒不退让，遂引申为「纠缠不休」，后进入法律术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run on two tracks: the animal itself, and the human pestering the baiting sport bequeathed, from reporters to courtrooms to slang swindles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八义项沿两条线索：动物本身，以及逗獾游戏留下的人际纠缠——从记者追问到法庭盘问再到俚语骗局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a striped face that will not let go, in the earth or at your elbow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张条纹脸不肯松口——无论在土里还是在你身边。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL SIDE: the mammal, the emblem, the stubborn neighbor.
branches.cn: 动物一面：獾本身、其象征、倔强的邻居。

branches.en: THE SPORT SIDE: the baiting pit where the verb was born.
branches.cn: 游戏一面：动词的诞生地——逗獾场。

branches.en: THE PESTERING SIDE: questions and requests without end.
branches.cn: 纠缠一面：没有穷尽的追问与请求。

branches.en: THE LEGAL SIDE: badgering the witness.
branches.cn: 法律一面：对证人的纠缠式盘问。

branches.en: THE SLANG SIDE: the swindle named for cornering.
branches.cn: 俚语一面：以围堵命名的骗局。

intro.en: Badger carries no living affix; its structure is a simple animal name turned verb.
intro.cn: badger 不含活跃词缀，其结构是单纯的动物名转动词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin enters here: the word is wholly English in formation, whatever its ultimate source.
latinIntro.cn: 与拉丁语无关：无论最终来源为何，构词全然是英语的。

items.example: an old sett in the wood

items.meaning: the sport of setting dogs on an animal

items.exampleCN: 被缠得不胜其烦的官员
